title: address-carrying man-memory n=16: identical tiles, address in B

regions.name: input
regions.note: the problem's own stream: `0 addr` (READ) / `1 addr value` (WRITE)

regions.name: router / broadcaster
regions.note: `r` the op and `X` on it, then broadcast exactly three words: addr, op, value. A READ has no value, so it sends a dummy 0 — fixed width means an unselected decoder needs no branch to know how much to swallow. This room owns no other outgoing pipe on purpose: `S` would broadcast into it too.

regions.name: decoder room
regions.note: all 16 decoders share this room, three rows each, every tile the same text. A decoder's `B` is his address and holds nothing else, which is the whole reason he exists: `~` needs `B`, and a cell's `B` is busy.

regions.name: cell room
regions.note: all 16 values share this room. A cell holds its value in `B` and never sees an address — it is addressed by which pipe speaks to it, and only its own decoder ever does.

regions.name: decoder addr 0
regions.note: B = 0 for life. `r` the broadcast address, `~` it against B: 0 only here. `X` straight = mine (forward op and value down), clockwise = not mine (swallow both, climb home east of the mine lane).

regions.name: cell addr 0
regions.note: value in B. READ: swallow the dummy, `W M s` sends it and puts it back. WRITE: `r` the value, `M` stores it. Never blocks anyone else — its decoder only speaks when this address is called.

regions.name: collector
regions.note: `R` reads from ANY incoming pipe, so the answer needs no addressing at all. Spanning the field is what makes every answer pipe a two-cell stub.

regions.name: output
regions.note: one word per READ

circles.name: the increment
circles.note: `+` with A=1 pinned: A = 1 + B. Then `M` puts it back in B and `1` restores A, so the next `Y` hands out the next address. This is the only difference between the two rooms' spawners.
